Subject: DPA: backup/DR retention carve-out request + eSign timeline

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. Legal here at Atlas Health has a few DPA points we need to confirm before we can sign: primarily a carve-out allowing longer backup retention for certain regulated records (patient-adjacent metadata), and an explicit DR restore window for emergency restores.

Key asks from our side:
- Allow backup retention beyond standard deletion window for regulated records up to 7 years (only for archived snapshots, with strict access controls).
- A defined process for emergency restores (DR) that may require retrieval of backups older than the normal retention window; documented authorization flow required.
- Confirmation Redwood will not use the data for model training and that subprocessors handling backups are listed.

We attached our redline (Atlas_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited carve-out and how you prefer to handle signature execution (DocuSign/AdobeSign)? We need target execution by end of July to meet our procurement deadlines.

Appreciate a short plan and timeline.

Best,
Sara Dunne
Sr. Counsel, Atlas Health

Subject: Re: DPA: backup/DR retention carve-out request + eSign timeline

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the detailed redlines and for flagging the timeline. Short answer: we can accept a narrowly scoped backup/DR carve-out but need to lock down operational limits and subprocessors. Proposed plan: 

1) Redwood counter with a limited carve-out: archived backups containing regulated records can be retained up to 7 years but only in encrypted, access-restricted cold storage; restores require documented Atlas authorization (two-person approval from Atlas security + Redwood CS manager).

2) Operational cap: Redwood will support emergency restores for backups up to 2 years by standard playbook; restores beyond 2 years are possible but are considered a manual, paid-for service with a 10 business day SLA. This avoids open-ended operational burden.

3) Subprocessors: we will include a subprocessor addendum listing our current backup/replication providers; we can provide FedRAMP / SOC 2 attestations where applicable.

4) Execution: suggest DocuSign for speed — I can upload a Redwood counter-redline. If you prefer AdobeSign, we can do that as well.

Looping in Rachel (Legal) and Karthik (Platform) to confirm the legal and ops wording. If legal signs off, I’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope and aim to have it ready for signature within 48 hours. Does that timeline work?

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Stephanie / Sara —

Reviewed the Atlas redline and Stephanie’s proposed counter. From a legal/compliance perspective, a few clarifications we should include in the counter to make the carve-out acceptable to Redwood and auditable for Atlas: 

- Scoped definition: replace general “regulated records” term with a defined data class (e.g., PHI-equivalent metadata) and require Atlas to flag datasets subject to the carve-out via an agreed manifest.
- Retention vs. backup: state explicitly that backups are immutable snapshots used only for restore purposes; normal data deletion requests will be honored for the primary dataset where feasible.
- DR authorization: require a documented request template plus two Atlas approvers (security officer + legal) before any restore occurs.
- Cost/ops: the manual restore beyond 180 days should be billed per-incident (we can include an estimate range).
- Subprocessor transparency: we will provide the current list and 30 days’ notice for changes; for any new subprocessor materially handling backups, Redwood will provide SOC 2 report or equivalent.

If Atlas is okay with the manifest approach and the 180-day standard restore window (with paid restore after that), I can approve the redline and we’ll put it in DocuSign for signature. 

Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara —

Thanks for working through this. Per Rachel and Karthik’s input, we have the following agreed changes to the DPA: 

- Scope: Carve-out limited to Atlas-flagged archived snapshots (manifest required).
- Retention: Archived snapshots may be retained up to 7 years in encrypted cold storage.
- Restore windows: Standard automated restores up to 180 days; manual, billable restores between 181 days and 2 years (5–10 business day SLA); restores >2 years are by exception and require scheduling.
- Authorization: Two-authorizer requirement from Atlas (security + legal) and Redwood CS manager sign-off for any restore.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will attach current subprocessor list and provide SOC 2 reports on request.

I’ve uploaded the agreed counter-redline to DocuSign and created an envelope for Atlas to sign. Please review and sign using the link below when ready: 

DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/XYZ-ATL-1192

Thanks again — aiming to close this today to hit your procurement window.
